full_judgment: He submits that the High Court Division erred in law in arriving at a erroneous decision by holding that the right of pre-emption of Shafi-e-jar based on vicinage under the Mohammadan Law is unconstitutional and offends Article 42(1) of the Constitution mainly relying upon a judgment of the Indian supreme Court reported in AIR 1962(SC) 1476, which was based on the secular nature of the Indian Constitution and is never sympathetic to retention of the Muslim Personal Laws in the country. Whereas our constitution vitally differs from the Indian Constitution on this issue. Constitution has expressly protected Muslim Person Laws along with personal laws of other communities but he learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in appreciating the basic difference and was enamored by the so-called secularistic idea and this approach to the case has vitiated the whole decision. He lastly submits that in any view of the matter, the judgment of the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal, but the High Court Division having arrived at an erroneous decision that Muslim Personal Law for Pre-emption is ultra-vires the Constitution and the court as bent on marshaling the evidences to fit in with the erroneous view. The Judges have grossly misinterpreted the statutes and failed to consider that Talab-I Mowsibat and Talab-I-Ishad were duly performed and the suit was filed within one year from the completion of the sale. Moreover, the learned Judges were wrong to hold that the plaintiff-petitioners failed to prove their title over the contiguous land and also the vicinity and the necessity of the suit land. Whereas, the learned Judge ought to have held that the plaintiff-petitioner No.2 is a natural person who confesses Muslim faith and is the beneficiary of the plaintiff-petitioner No.1 company as being the majority shareholder of the company and the trial court decreed the suit deciding all the issues in favour of the plaintiff but the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law and traveled beyond the relevant issues and committed gross illegalities which requires interference by this Court."
